jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
Wendel, an Esri Business Partner and multi‑disciplinary Architectural and Engineering firm, is seeking an experienced part‑time, provisional GIS Analyst for a short‑term engagement. The position will be based out of the Williamsville, New York office, with flexibility for candidates located near other Wendel office locations. This role is focused on ArcGIS Enterprise administration, spatial web services, and cloud-hosted GIS solutions supporting companywide projects across multiple disciplines. The analyst will collaborate directly with the GIS Manager, Developers, and Project Managers to deliver enterprise-level geospatial infrastructure and analyses.

Responsibilities

Administer ArcGIS Enterprise (Portal for ArcGIS, Data Store) within virtualized server environments
Publish, manage, and maintain hosted feature layers through ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, ensuring performance and availability of REST service endpoints.
Build and maintain web mapping applications using ArcGIS Experience Builder, Web AppBuilder, etc.
Convert and integrate GIS data to/from CAD formats and perform advanced spatial analysis (buffering, overlays, network analysis, distance calculations).
Manage mobile field data collection workflows using ArcGIS Field Maps and Survey123, including form design and data synchronization with enterprise hosted layers.
Support the GIS Developer with SQL database administration to automate workflows
Conduct client training on web applications, GPS collection, and enterprise GIS workflows for internal and external stakeholders

Qualifications

B.A. or B.S. in Geography, GIS, or related field.
3+ years of professional GIS experience.
Demonstrated ArcGIS Enterprise administration experience (Portal, Server, Data Store).
Experience working with GIS infrastructure in virtualized server environments
Proficient in Esri's full ArcGIS suite including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and Enterprise Portal.
Experience publishing and managing REST services (map, feature, image, and geoprocessing)
Strong working knowledge of SDE geodatabases
Proficient in Python scripting with ArcPy for automation of publishing workflows, data processing, and geodatabase management.
Strong understanding of REST API architecture and experience troubleshooting service endpoints.
Experience with coordinate systems, projections, and spatial reference management at an enterprise scale.
Experience with mobile data collection platforms: ArcGIS Survey123 and ArcGIS Field Maps.
Demonstrated ability to produce publication-quality maps, figures, and visuals for project deliverables.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently and on a team.

Hourly Range: $32.21 - $59.13

Wendel is committed to providing fair, competitive, and market-informed compensation. The rate offered will be determined based off the successful candidates’ relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. The rate offered will also take into consideration regional adjustment factors.

This is a part‑time, provisional position with a short‑term appointment. Hours and duration will be determined based on project scope and mutual agreement. Candidates with experience in ArcGIS Enterprise administration and virtual server environments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Hear from Our Team:
We asked our employees to share what they love most about working at Wendel, and the overwhelming response was that everyone loves working in an environment where the team has each other’s backs. They also liked our flexible, hybrid work policy. With nationwide project and office locations, Wendel presents the opportunity to work on an exciting variety of projects with a diverse group of clients. They said they like our respect-based and team-oriented culture, and our transparent communication philosophy.

Helping our employees reach their professional goals is important to us, and we take pride in providing a variety of professional development opportunities. We utilize an annual career development process, for every employee that ensures career mobility, growth, and company ownership potential.

Don’t meet every single requirement? We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Wendel is an Affirmative Action, Equal Opportunity Employer and provides a drug-free workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, genetic information, citizenship status, or any other basis prohibited by law. Generate regular data summaries tracking volume and system processing speeds and error rates.

Regularly review quantitative and qualitative data to evaluate program outcomes and use them to identify opportunities for improvement and assist in implementation as needed.

Cross-check submitted affidavit details to ensure e-bike retailer and consumer compliance with program rules.
Flag duplicate submissions, suspicious data patterns, or non-compliant affidavits for team review.
Perform routine compliance reviews across processed records to maintain high data accuracy and program integrity.
General Responsibilities (10%)
Work with the Office of Information Technology (OIT) and others on software and services procurement and/or related invoicing.
Maintain up-to-date standard operating procedures (SOPs) and documentation for all data handling, software use and validation tasks.
Perform other administrative support, meeting participation and duties as needed to support the E-Mobility team within CEO’s Transportation department.

A mission-driven organization is using data, research, and evidence to tackle some of the most complex challenges facing communities and public systems.

Its work spans areas including housing, maternal health, public safety, benefits delivery, and other complex social and public-policy challenges.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Program Analyst to serve as an embedded analytical partner to one or more program teams.

This is not a traditional reporting role where you’ll receive clean datasets and clearly defined analytical requests. You’ll learn the strategy, stakeholders, datasets, and recurring decisions behind a program area and help determine what questions should be asked, what data exists to answer them, and what conclusions the evidence can legitimately support.
A significant portion of the work involves finding and evaluating external and publicly available data, combining it with internal information, and working through messy, incomplete, or unfamiliar datasets.

You’ll use Python, R, and SQL
to clean, analyze, model, validate, and reproduce your work. Just as importantly, you’ll need the analytical judgment to challenge assumptions, choose appropriate methodologies, understand limitations, and turn your findings into recommendations that leaders can act on.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys taking an ambiguous question from initial data discovery all the way through analysis, validation, communication, and decision support.

What You’ll Do

Become deeply familiar with the strategy, stakeholders, datasets, and recurring decisions of the program areas you support.
Serve as an embedded analytical partner to program leaders.
Identify analytical needs and opportunities before they become formal requests.
Turn broad or ambiguous questions into structured, answerable analytical problems.
Challenge assumptions and determine the smallest useful analysis required to support a decision.
Find and evaluate external, public, and administrative datasets.
Combine messy data from multiple sources and assess its quality, reliability, and limitations.
Use Python, R, and SQL to clean, analyze, model, validate, and reproduce analytical work.
Build reproducible models, analyses, prototypes, and recurring analytical products.
Apply sound methodological judgment to data discovery, analytical design, validation, interpretation, and recommendations.
Clearly communicate what available data can—and cannot—support.
Translate analysis into concise decision memos, briefs, visualizations, and presentations.
Present findings and recommendations to program leaders and nontechnical stakeholders.
Work quickly across unfamiliar subject areas while maintaining analytical rigor.
Use AI-assisted tools for research, coding, quality assurance, and documentation while independently validating the work.
Contribute to analytical standards, peer review, and documentation across a small Strategic Analytics team.

What You Bring

Approximately 3–5 years of applied analytical experience, with additional relevant experience welcomed.
A strong quantitative foundation through STEM, economics, applied quantitative social science, or comparable demonstrated analytical experience.
Professional experience using Python and R
for real analytical work.
Working SQL experience and the ability to query and manipulate data independently.
Experience building reproducible analyses rather than relying exclusively on manual or one-off work.
Experience working with messy, incomplete, unstructured, or unfamiliar datasets.
Experience finding and evaluating data rather than only working with established internal datasets.
Ability to combine public/external data with internal information to answer complex questions.
Experience taking an ambiguous question through data discovery, methodology selection, validation, interpretation, and recommendation.
Strong analytical judgment and an understanding of what conclusions available evidence can reasonably support.
Ability to assess data quality, document limitations, and explain methodological decisions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience translating technical analysis into practical recommendations for nontechnical decision-makers.
High degree of ownership, curiosity, and comfort operating without a predefined analytical roadmap.

Especially Valuable

Strategy consulting, economic consulting, boutique analytics consulting, startup, or similarly fast-moving analytical experience.
Experience working with public or administrative datasets.
Housing analytics.
Maternal health analytics.
Public safety or criminal justice analytics.
Geospatial analysis.
Data visualization.
Experience supporting public-sector, nonprofit, social-impact, or policy-related decision-making.

Prior nonprofit experience is not required.

What Makes Someone Successful Here

The strongest candidates won't simply know how to code.

You should be comfortable receiving a question that isn't fully defined, determining what data is available, finding additional sources, assessing whether those sources are reliable, choosing an appropriate analytical approach, and building a reproducible analysis in Python or R.

You'll need to make independent judgment calls about what the evidence actually supports rather than forcing the data toward a predetermined answer.

From there, you should be able to explain your findings clearly, document your methodology and limitations, and turn the analysis into something a program leader can use to make a decision.

Why Join?

This is an opportunity to apply rigorous analytics to complex, real-world problems where the work can directly influence programs, investments, and decisions.

Rather than sitting several steps removed from stakeholders, you'll work closely with program leaders and become an analytical partner in their decision-making.

You'll join a small Strategic Analytics team where intellectual curiosity, methodological rigor, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn messy evidence into practical recommendations are highly valued.
